entertainment.title: 10 Cartoons Every Star Trek Fan Needs To Watch
entertainment.summary: The Star Trek franchise has influenced a plethora of great sci-fi projects over the years, including several of the genre's best animated series.
entertainment.body:
Paramount+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover When it comes to setting the bar for science fiction on television, Star Trek still stands as the gold standard. The long-running franchise's influence can be felt extensively in the medium, including in animated shows that similarly explore the cosmos. Star Trek has, of course, created its own set of cartoons complementing the franchise's growing legacy of live-action programming. It's those shows that we're spotlighting here, the cartoons that feel the closest to Star Trek or extensions of the live-action franchise themselves.

The types of animated shows that we're highlighting here all revolve around characters traversing space and time for their own purposes. In some cases, spacefaring exploration is the key, while others involve cosmically scaled adventures with less noble motives. But all of the shows that we mention here feature high-concept sci-fi on full display as a narrative constant. Here are 10 cartoons every Star Trek fan needs to watch, each evoking similar science fiction vibes.

CBS Studios Let's get the most obvious inclusion out of the way first with "Star Trek: The Animated Series," which ran for two seasons from 1973 to 1974. The show features most of the main cast from "Star Trek: The Original Series" returning to reprise their roles as the crew of the Enterprise on its five-year exploratory mission. The show explores key parts of the established mythos, with some episodes serving as direct sequels to previous "TOS" stories. The series also contains the first Holodeck episode, over a decade before "The Next Generation" debuted .

"The Animated Series" has become an influential, if still widely overlooked, part of the overall Star Trek franchise. Through the possibilities of animation, the show could take on stories that would've likely been too cost-prohibitive for its live-action predecessor to produce. The show also gives fans a chance to see the classic cast reprise their iconic roles, albeit as '70s cartoon characters. Underrated in the quality of its sci-fi storytelling, some of the best Star Trek episodes in franchise history were told by "The Animated Series."

Academy Productions Anime has had its own longstanding history with space opera and interstellar science fiction for decades, with one of the most foundational being "Space Battleship Yamato." Debuting in 1974, the show is named for a spaceship sent on a desperate mission across the cosmos after Earth is irradiated during a war with an extraterrestrial empire. The Yamato's mission is to recover a device from a faraway planet capable of saving their home world from the lethal fallout. The show was followed by sequel series in 1978 and 1980, with the Yamato dealing with new threats from the far reaches of outer space.

Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in such a short amount of time. He first topped the chart a little more than six years ago — on Aug. 15, 2020.

I’m the Problem is Wallen’s third album to log a full year at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Dangerous: The Double Album clung to the top spot for 97 weeks from 2021-23. One Thing at a Time led for 87 weeks from 2023-25. No other artist has spent 52 weeks on top with one album, much less three.

Top Country Albums originated as Hot Country Albums in the Jan. 11, 1964 issue of Billboard . Johnny Cash ’s Ring of Fire (The Best of Johnny Cash) headed the inaugural chart. The compilation was well-timed: “Ring of Fire” had headed Hot Country Songs for seven weeks the previous summer and had crossed over to reach the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The chart was named Hot Country LP’s from 1968 to 1984, when vinyl LPs were king.

Twenty-one artists have logged 50 or more weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Male solo artists dominate, as you might expect, though three female solo artists have achieved the feat, as have two groups. (One of those groups is an all-female group.) entertainment.title: Twilight Zone Creator Rod Serling Said TV Sponsors Ruined One Of His Early Stories
entertainment.summary: Before The Twilight Zone, Rod Serling wrote a story that he hoped would tackle a truly insidious issue in America - and it never made it past the sponsor.
entertainment.body:
In 1956, Serling wrote a story for "The United States Steel Hour," an anthology series sponsored by U.S. Steel. Titled "Noon on Doomsday," the episode in question is about a prejudiced community that circles the wagon to protect its own in the wake of a killing, much as Mississippi did after the murderers of 14-year-old Till walked free. Serling's initial draft featured a Jewish victim, because he preemptively assumed sponsors and censors would object to the explicit Black-and-white racial allegory.

As it turned out, even that was too provocative; White Citizens Councils in the South threatened a boycott, and U.S. Steel caved. Now, the victim was just some unnamed foreigner, though it was apparently preferred they not be coded as a minority at all. The word "lynch" couldn't be said in the episode, either. The setting was moved to New England, and Coca-Cola bottles were even removed from the set because of the "Southern connotations." Serling later joked, grimly, to Mike Wallace that the powers-that-be would have set it at the North Pole if the costumes hadn't prevented them from doing so.

In 1958, Serling tried to tell a story inspired by Emett Till's lynching again, this time on CBS's "Playhouse 90." ( William Shatner, who would later lead two "Twilight Zone" episodes , starred.) While his initial draft featured a Black character, the network objected once more. "By the time 'A Town Has Turned to Dust' went before the cameras, my script had turned to dust," Serling said, according to the Dayton Daily News . "Emmitt Till became a romantic Mexican. The setting was moved to the Southwest in the 1870s ... they chopped it up like a roomful of butchers at work on a street."

Despite the heavy censorship, reviewers at the time praised the story's message. Drama students at Ithaca College, where Serling used to teach, performed a reading of the original draft in 2008.

entertainment.title: Mahershala Ali Says “There Are Not Roles for Me” in “Vast Majority of Projects,” Despite Winning 2 Oscars
entertainment.summary: The actor previously took home Academy Awards for best supporting actor for 2016’s 'Moonlight' and 2018's 'Green Book.'
entertainment.body:
Mahershala Ali is getting candid about why “there are not roles” for him in “the vast majority of projects,” despite having already won two Oscars.

During a recent interview on Carmelo Anthony and Kazeem “Kaz” Famuyide’s 7PM in Brooklyn podcast , the actor — who previously took home Academy Awards for best supporting actor for 2016’s Moonlight and 2018’s Green Book — opened up about how earning Hollywood’s highest recognition doesn’t guarantee access to great roles.

“There’s a lot of great actors that don’t have Oscars, who are also looking for good material,” he said. “And that’s no disrespect to The Academy or the award at all, but what I’m actually saying is that Oscar or no Oscar, there’s a lot of good actors out there. There’s more good actors than there is good material.” Related Stories Movies Katelin Arizmendi on Bringing a New Perspective to Action With 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' Movies Mahershala Ali Put His Two Oscars Into a Cabinet: "I Felt a Sense of Accomplishment, Not Fulfillment"

“It’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots. It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes. And then you got to be right for it,” Ali continued. “The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.”

Given the current political climate, Ali later added that rollbacks of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) funding and initiatives also “on some level impact what gets greenlit.”

“I don’t know how much of an impact it has, but I just know that if certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world we live in, they’ll just keep centering who they see in their offices, and it ain’t a bunch of us in those offices,” he said.

The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star explained that the only other option for actors is to produce and create their own projects; however, “that’s a five-year journey itself.”

Famuyide later asked Ali about the fan notion that Black actors are “validated” only after winning an Oscar. “It’s kind of just talk. It doesn’t translate to anything real,” the actor replied.

entertainment.title: ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With ‘GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’
entertainment.summary: Plus, U2 achieves its 14th top 10 with the debut of Carnaval de Luz .
entertainment.body:
ATEEZ earn their fourth No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart as GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 debuts atop the tally (dated Nov. 28). It’s the 10th top 10-charted project for the act, all of which have come since 2022. With the arrival, ATEEZ stand alone as the group with the most top 10s in the 2020s. Among all acts this decade, only YoungBoy Never Broke Again (15) and Taylor Swift (14) have more.

GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 bows with 195,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the week ending Nov. 19, largely driven by pure album sales (191,000).

Also in the top 10, U2 collects its 14th top 10 as the band’s new studio album, Carnaval de Luz , debuts at No. 4.

The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Nov. 28, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard ‘s website on Nov. 24. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X, formerly known as Twitter, and Instagram.

Of GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 ’s 195,000 first-week equivalent album units, album sales comprise 191,000 (it debuts at No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart), SEA units comprise 4,000 (equaling 4.04 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise a negligible sum.

ATEEZ have logged their 10 top 10s on the Billboard 200 consecutively. The act claimed its first top 10 with the No. 3-peaking THE WORLD EP.1 : MOVEMENT in 2022. In total, with 10 top 10s in the 2020s, ATEEZ now solely have the most top 10s among groups this decade. The act was previously tied with Stray Kids (which got its ninth top 10 — and ninth No. 1 — in August with This & That ).

GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 ’s album sales were bolstered by its availability across 32 CD and vinyl variants (all containing collectible items such as photocards and posters, with some items randomized), including signed editions.

Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love falls to No. 2 on the latest Billboard 200 with 62,000 equivalent album units earned (down 1%). Morgan Wallen’s chart-topping I’m the Problem is a non-mover at No. 3 with a little more than 49,000 (up less than 1%).

During the matchup at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City—which marked Travis’ 100th regular season home game—the NFL star scored not one, but two career-defining touchdowns while dominating the field. In the game’s first quarter, his touchdown launched him into third place all-time for the most career touchdowns by an NFL tight end, which was followed by a second touchdown that marked his first two-touchdown game since 2022.

And it was clear that Taylor and Wyatt—the eldest daughter of the “Opalite” singer’s in-laws Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce ’s four kids—were in a state of grace over the achievement as footage shared to social media Nov. 22 caught them in a sweet embrace after the second play.

The 36-year-old—donning a Chiefs windbreaker from Erin Andrews ’ WEAR clothing line and her signature red lip—yelled in excitement from her suite as she hugged Wyatt from behind.

And it’s clear Wyatt was thrilled to have her aunt wrapped around her like a cardigan as she smiled wide.

But they weren’t the only ones enchanted by Travis’ skills on the field. After all, the athlete did a little celebrating himself after his 22-yard touchdown reception, yelling “come on!” as he jumped up and down.

entertainment.title: Before Mad Men, Jon Hamm Was A High School Teacher Who Taught This Future Co-Star
entertainment.summary: Early in his career, Jon Hamm taught drama in a Missouri high school. Years later, he would go on to star alongside one of his former students in a hit show.
entertainment.body:
Featureflash Photo Agency/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover There are plenty of teachers out there who can fondly remember when they had a future celebrity in their class, but not many of them can say they became famous alongside one of their own students. Such is the case with Jon Hamm. Long before he would become a household name as Don Draper on "Mad Men," one of the best AMC shows of all time , Hamm spent a year as a drama teacher at his old high school in Missouri. As it turns out, one of his students that year would eventually become one of his co-stars: Ellie Kemper.

On " The Kelly Clarkson Show ," Hamm explains how he ended up there. "In 2004, after I graduated college, I had a theater degree and no prospects. So I was like, well, what can I do?" he said. "I know, I'll talk to my old acting teacher and maybe he'll gimme a job teaching at my old high school,"

In an interview on " Andy Cohen Live ," Kemper admitted she had a bit of a crush on her future celeb teacher. "So, he's 10 years older than I am." Kemper said. "And he's the youngest teacher by far. He's not bad looking, and he's teaching drama. He's in fact great looking. Dreamy."

Hamm lasted one season at the school before moving on to pursue his acting career. Eventually, the two of them would appear together in the Netflix series "Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt," where Kemper played a woman who's freed from an underground bunker, held captive by Hamm.

Netflix Ellie Kemper says even after being her teacher, Jon Hamm continued to help her. "I was doing this one-person show in Los Angeles, and at that time, he was already famous on 'Mad Men,'" she said on "Andy Cohen Live." "I emailed him from our high school directory. I said, 'Hey, I'm doing this show. I know you're really busy, but it'd be great if you could come.' And he came, and that's when I reconnected with him."

Hamm and Kemper formed a friendship after that. On an episode of " Live with Kelly and Mark ," he said he could tell she had star potential way back in high school. "Even at 15, she was an incredibly composed, very smart, hardworking actress," he said. That potential led to Kemper's addition to the cast of "The Office" as one of the dumbest characters ever and eventually "Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt," one of several Netflix shows without a bad season .

It was his friendship with Kemper and prior working relationship with show creator Tina Fey that helped Hamm land the role of Kimmy's captor. In a 2015 interview with the Television Critics Association, Kemper said working with him was a little scary at first. "Acting with him was a little bit nerve-racking just because I felt like he was still grading me on some level," she said per People . "But he's a wonderful man and it was a lot of fun."

entertainment.title: PlaqueBoyMax Wants to Find Your Next Favorite Artist
entertainment.summary: With his music competition, "Rising Star," the streamer is giving emerging artists a weekend to show what they can do. He’s got an album of his own in the works, too
entertainment.body:
It’s been about a year and a half since rapper and streamer PlaqueboyMax first spoke to Rolling Stone . In that time, the music industry has caught up with the popularity of streamers, as a growing set of major names — from Drake to Mariah Carey — have dabbled in the format. For Max, who has spent years making music in front of viewers, that means being something of an established figure in an evolving rap landscape.

“It’s been crazy,” he says. “I’m really passionate about music, and I’m just happy that I’m able to merge my worlds and my passions together to make it one big world.”

Max’s recent “Rising Star” competition, something like Star Search or American Idol for the underground rap generation, brought together six rappers with growing fanbases on one livestream where they’d create music and eventually perform for a real audience. The contest has its origins in two of Max’s streaming formats. “In the Booth,” which he started in 2024, lets viewers watch music being made. He was also doing “Song Wars” around then, putting songs up for an audience’s judgment. As he kept doing those streams, he wanted to spend more time with the artists. What else would people want to know about somebody they’d just watched make a song?

“These are concepts where people are making songs and new art is being created live,” he says. “It’s very fascinating. And ‘Rising Star’ is basically a byproduct of these things, but taken even further.”

The weekend format lets the audience spend hours with the contestants, who have personalities and frustrations to contend with as they’re making music. Max would like some of that audience to stick with them afterward.

“My whole premise with ‘Rising Star’ is that I want to find artists of the next generation that are coming up now, as opposed to maybe an already established artist and allow them to showcase what they’re doing and what they’re capable of and who they are as artists through this event.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

He recruited Lil Yachty, with his years of experience making records and maintaining a career, alongside creators Cuffem and Funny Marco. Music advice from the rapper, entertainment from the creators: Max wanted both on the panel, with enough to keep his viewers watching.

“So I would say picking judges came down [to] just me picking people I appreciate, who I mess with, and just bringing them into my world and making it all one amazing product,” he says.

entertainment.title: Chuck Lorre's First Sitcom Is A Forgotten Show That's Impossible To Watch Today
entertainment.summary: Before his name became synonymous with successful sitcoms thanks to "Two and a Half Men," Chuck Lorre created a show that is basically lost media now.
entertainment.body:
Christopher Polk/Polk Imaging for Penske Media Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Before he was the "King of Sitcoms" (per Reuters ) behind the television juggernauts "The Big Bang Theory" and "Two and a Half Men," one of Chuck Lorre's first jobs — besides working on several kids' cartoons you didn't know Lorre worked on — was as a staff writer for "Roseanne." According to The New Yorker , his work impressed the producers enough to earn him the opportunity to create his own show: "Frannie's Turn." It premiered on September 13, 1992, and was canceled just five short weeks later. Not only was the sitcom short-lived, but it has also become impossible to watch today.

Given its brief run, the show has never received a DVD or Blu-ray release, and you won't find it on any streaming services or legitimate (or even illegitimate) digital platforms. The only footage on YouTube is some CBS promos .

"Frannie's Turn" is about, as Lorre says, "a fifty-year-old middle-class woman coming into her own" (via The New Yorker ). Similar to "Roseanne" or "Mama's Family," it focuses on a matriarch with a chaotic home life trying to keep it all together. Miriam Margolyes stars as Frannie Escobar, a Staten Island seamstress who clashes with her old-fashioned and misogynistic Cuban-American husband, played by Tomás Milián, while she balances her deadbeat son (Stivi Paskoski), strong-willed daughter (Phoebe Augustine), and, of course, a zany mother-in-law (Alice Drummond).

Themes like female independence, generational and cultural differences, marital tension, and family dysfunction were meant to unfold over the course of the show. But CBS never gave it much of a chance, and it disappeared soon after it arrived. Of course, this was only a mere setback in what would become Chuck Lorre's storied career.

Matt Baron/Shutterstock If you're trying to find anything else about "Frannie's Turn," it will be incredibly difficult. Only a few of the plot summaries are available on IMDb. "Sex and Saints," episode three, was about how "Rosa claims to have encountered St. Monica, and though Frannie and Joseph dismiss her, they are unable to rule out divine intervention to improve their less-than-heavenly love life," while "Frannie and the Kitchen Sink," episode six, featured a much more mundane domestic dispute: "Frannie and Joseph fight over a leaky kitchen sink."

For the rest of the episodes, "The Pilot," "Money Talks," "Olivia Walks," "How Do You Say Death in Spanish?," and "Gentlemen, Wrap Your Guava," we will just have to dream up our own plots and guess what might have happened.

entertainment.title: 15 Best TV Comedy Shows Of The 2010s, Ranked
entertainment.summary: The 2010s were an exciting time for comedy on television, and these shows represent the best the genre had to offer during that decade.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The 2010s were a fantastic decade for television comedy, with a wide offering of both boundary-breaking experiments and more traditional, classically structured ensemble sitcoms that knew how to play to the genre's strengths in the post-prestige era. On this list, we'll be looking over the decade's 15 absolute best offerings of TV comedy, which occupy various different positions within that spectrum.

The ground rules of this list are that we're only looking at English-language live-action shows, and only taking into account seasons and episodes that aired between January 2010 and December 2019 — i.e., each show's output within the actual decade. For some, it didn't take more than a handful of episodes to stake out their place in the decade's canon.

Comedy Central One of the most deranged, unbound, and envelope-pushing American comedy series of the 2010s, Comedy Central's "Review" was developed by Andy Daly, Jeffrey Blitz, and Charlie Siskel as an adaptation of Australia's "Review with Myles Barlow," and stars Daly as Forrest MacNeil. The host of a fictional documentary series on which he endeavors to engage in miscellaneous viewer-requested activities and then assign each one a rating between one and five stars, Forrest is so single-mindedly committed to his show's ethos that he will try out absurd, dangerous, degrading, and unreasonably taxing experiences so long as someone asks — even to the detriment of his own life.

"Review" is a masterpiece of the kind of absurdist, dark-silly comedy that arguably defined its decade; not for nothing, it's one of the best Comedy Central shows of all time . The series' effervescence in mining its pseudo-reality-TV setup for satirical bite and exploring its own outlandish scenarios to the last consequences is only matched by the relentless hilarity of every single episode — attributable in no small part to the impeccable performance of Daly as the poor fool at the center of the carnival.

The CW With apologies to "Glee," the great English-language musical comedy series of the 2010s is The CW's "Crazy Ex-Girlfriend." With two or more great to spectacular original songs and lavish accompanying musical numbers per episode, the Rachel Bloom and Aline Brosh McKenna-created series follows Rebecca Bunch (Bloom), a New York City lawyer who abruptly decides to revamp her entire life and move to West Covina, Calif., after a chance encounter with her ex-boyfriend, Josh Chan (Vincent Rodriguez III) — all while insisting that she's not moving there to follow him.

One of the longest-running shows in American TV history , "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" is filled to the brim with shocking plot twists and episodes that could never be made today due to their subject matter. One of the most frustrating realities of a series that lasts this long is that storylines are occasionally dropped without any explanation. Writers and executive producers don't always control when an actor decides to leave a show, so the only thing that can be done sometimes is to explain an exit with a quick line that can feel narratively unsatisfying — or, in some cases, do absolutely nothing at all.

"SVU" also follows a traditional "case of the week" formula, so the end of an episode is often purposefully ambiguous, even if it makes more sense to keep following the story. The show ultimately focuses on the personal lives of the team at the 16th Precinct, whether they intersect with cases or not. Whether they involved Captain Olivia Benson's (Mariska Hargitay) personal life, relationships among detectives, or a case that spanned several episodes, these five stories were completely abandoned by "Law & Order: SVU."

entertainment.title: Princess Kate enforces simple household rules to keep royal kids grounded: author
entertainment.summary: Kate Middleton's approach to chores echoes Queen Elizabeth, who once insisted on washing up at Balmoral
entertainment.body:
Being born into royalty doesn’t mean getting a free pass at home.

Kate Middleton is reportedly determined to make sure Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis don’t grow up expecting everything to be done for them. And the future queen consort has a surprisingly ordinary way of keeping her three children grounded.

“When it comes to household chores, Kate is extremely organized,” Christopher Andersen, author of “Kate!,” told Fox News Digital, citing his own sources. “She wants to impart her ingrained sense of normalcy to the children by having them do all their own chores. There is a schedule that she draws up and posts in the kitchen, dividing up daily tasks among the kids.”

“They make their own beds every morning, prepare their own breakfasts and clean up after themselves,” said Andersen. “It’s a good thing that Prince George was accustomed to making his own bed at home, because that’s one of the chores he’s expected to do at Eton College. It’s a valuable lesson for any child growing up under such abnormal circumstances.”

Fox News Digital reached out to Kensington Palace for comment. A palace spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital that the palace does not comment on books.

Kate has made no secret of her fondness for one household chore in particular.

“I love washing up. I really do,” the princess said during a visit to a community transport organization in West Sussex.

When asked whether William lends a helping hand, Kate replied, “He does the drying. We are a good double act. And we get the children involved,” The Times of London reported.

entertainment.title: Legendary Jewelry Designer Paolo Bulgari Dead at 89
entertainment.summary: The fashion world has lost a legend. Paolo Bulgari—famed jewelry designer and chairman of the Bvlgari Group—has died, the company confirmed on social media Nov. 21. He was 89. “It is with deep...
entertainment.body:
Paolo Bulgari —famed jewelry designer and chairman of the Bvlgari Group—has died, the company confirmed on social media Nov. 21. He was 89.

“It is with deep sadness that we learned of the passing of Paolo Bulgari, grandson of the company’s founder Sotirio Bulgari and Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984,” the company said in a statement shared to Instagram. “Our deepest condolences go to his family, friends and all those who had the honor of sharing this journey with him.”

“Thank you, Mr. Paolo,” they added, “your legacy as a brilliant beacon of creative inspiration will continue to inspire generations to come.”

Born in Rome, Italy, in 1937, Bulgari—who shared four kids with ex-wife Alice Valli as well as two kids with wife Maite Caprio —was destined to carry on the family business from a young age.

“Paolo Bulgari began collaborating with his father in 1960,” the statement explained, “specializing in the knowledge of precious stones, of which he was one of the world’s leading experts, and refining the sensibility and aesthetic sense that are at the root of the Bvlgari style.”

And it wasn’t long until he started making his own mark on the brand.

“A true creative soul, he poured his heart into his craft and into nurturing the talents of young designers,” added the statement, “leaving an indelible mark on the world of jewelry.”

In fact, Bulgari, alongside his brothers Gianni Bulgari and Nicola Bulgari , played an integral role in shaping the brand’s distinctive style, becoming known for their use of bold shapes and standout gems.

entertainment.title: Tom Jackson, Former NFL Player And Longtime ESPN Analyst, Dead At 75
entertainment.summary: Tom Jackson, a former player for the NFL's Denver Broncos who went on to become an award-winning ESPN commentator, has died.
entertainment.body:
An exact cause of death has yet to be reported, but ESPN's Chris Berman — who co-hosted multiple football-centric shows with Jackson on the network over the years — called his colleague's death "unexpected" while sharing the news during Sunday's "NFL Countdown" broadcast.

"He was a vital 75," Berman said. "Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock. ... I talked with him at length on Tuesday. We'd talk about life. We would talk about the world. Eventually, we'd get to football. Some conversations, we wouldn't."

Berman remarked that it was especially strange to be announcing Jackson's death on November 22, as that was the day President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in 1963. Berman and Jackson were both young during that historical event, and every year on that date, they would catch up "for five or 10 minutes" to remember the anniversary.

"Now I'm talking about Tom, who's gone, and I won't be able to have that conversation anymore," Berman said. You can watch his full announcement below:

"We've lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet."

Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson.

What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0eogqMa73r

Jackson joined ESPN's team of football analysts in 1987, and he co-hosted "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime" with Chris Berman for nearly 30 years. He retired from full-time hosting duties in 2016, but later returned in 2019 when "NFL Primetime" moved to the ESPN+ streaming service. That stint was ultimately short-lived, as Jackson stepped away in 2020 due to concerns over the COVID-19 pandemic; he was replaced at the desk by Anthony Darelle "Booger" McFarland, who remains a co-host now.

entertainment.body: Sarah Paulson is pulling back the curtain on her living arrangement with longtime partner Holland Taylor. “We met when I was already 40 and she was already 72,” Paulson, 51, said on the Monday, November 16, episode of “The Run-Through With Vogue” podcast. “Stories had been written and ways in which we moved through the world had been decided and she’s a really independent person.” Paulson and Taylor, 83, first crossed paths in 2005 at a party and later reconnected, confirming their romance one decade later. During Monday’s episode, Paulson recalled a moment “early on” in their relationship where she bought a house and “worried” whether it was atypical for her and Taylor not to be residing together. “When I was sort of like … ‘Is it weird that we are not living together?’” Paulson said. “She was like, ‘Well, you did just buy a house, so what are you asking me about it for as if it’s something I’m doing? You made that choice.’ I was like, ‘Oh, right. Well, I never owned a home. And I thought it would be good to do so.’” She continued, “I don’t even think about like, ‘Oh absence makes the heart go fonder’ — although I do think it does, and it can — but I also just think there is something about the respect for each other’s individual space. Where it’s like you don’t have to force it upon one another in order to be intimate and connected and together.” Paulson explained that her living situation with the Morning Show actress “feels really good” to her, while noting that it’s “not necessarily a traditional way of doing something.” “But neither is being with a person 32 years older than you, is not traditional either,” she added. “There’s something about the story that just is what it is. I’m not here to convince anybody why it works, why it doesn’t work, what works for me, why I like it, you know. But it’s great.” Paulson noted that she has currently been “cohabitating more” while dealing with “drama” surrounding coyotes on her property and navigating construction on her home. “She’s often in New York working or she’s in Texas shooting that show Brothers with Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. entertainment.title: The Hotel Bel-Air’s Menu Returns to Tradition
entertainment.summary: Everything old is new again, as classic hits are revived, from the Thai-style chicken salad to the house burger.
entertainment.body:
Since Wolfgang Puck’s 2023 departure from the Hotel Bel-Air and its eponymous restaurant, the luxury lodging has been tweaking its Cal-Med menus with classical French techniques and hyper-seasonal ingredients. The approach was ambitious, evolving, at times even experimental . Yet the largely local dining clientele — 70 percent of weekly regulars are neighbors — who treat the place as a second home (or maybe a fourth, given their net worth) have made it clear they prefer familiarity over ingenuity. Under new executive chef Ralf Schlegel (far left), previously of The Peninsula in Beverly Hills, the kitchen has turned back toward the classics.

The bill of fare has long had a dedicated section of “Bel-Air Classics”: the tortilla soup, the club sandwich, the chopped salad named for late No. 1 fan Nancy Reagan. Now, the restaurant has restored several other salads that had been relegated to off-menu, only-by-request status — Thai-style chicken, soy ginger BBQ salmon, burrata with squash — along with the house burger.

“When you go home, you want what you remember,” explains Hotel Bel-Air manager Tiffany Lai, who insists the restaurant’s back-to-basics pivot won’t condemn it to culinary ossification. “We’re still busy creating new favorites.” She points to the German-born, Austria-raised Schlegel’s signature dish: chicken schnitzel with lemon paprika (left). “Maybe in 15 years that’ll be the next classic.”

sports.title: Liam Coen: I was told ball switched hands on Parker Washington catch
sports.summary: The Giants held off the Jaguars on Sunday, but the outcome might have been different if referees had made a different ruling on a pass to Jaguars wideout Parker Washington early in the fourth quarter.
sports.body:
Washington appeared to make a diving catch in the back corner of the end zone, but officials on the field ruled that the pass was incomplete. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen challenged that Washington had control of the ball while inbounds, but the call was upheld on review.

After the game, Coen was asked if he received an explanation for the ruling by officials.

During the CBS broadcast of the game, officiating analyst Gene Steratore said that he spoke to the league office and that “they felt like there was not enough clear and obvious evidence to change the ruling on the field.”

Washington bobbled the ball briefly at first contact, but appeared to have established control by the time he hit the ground and maintained it after landing. The call went the other way in a consequential moment for the Jaguars, but an ill-timed turnover and Coen’s decisions later in the game also had a heavy hand in the final result at MetLife Stadium.

sports.title: Giants earn their most impressive win of the season with upset of Jaguars
sports.summary: The NFC East leaders surprised the AFC South leaders today.
sports.body:
In a game that few expected the Giants to win, New York took a 10-3 first quarter lead and never relinquished it, turning in an impressive performance and beating the Jaguars 23-18.

The Giants were aided by two highly controversial touchdown calls: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston got a fourth-and-goal tush push touchdown despite his helmet appearing to be down before the ball crossed the goal line, and Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington was denied a touchdown catch despite appearing to have possession with his feet down in bounds.

But the two controversies shouldn’t overshadow that this Giants team is far better than anyone expected. They’re 6-3-1 and in total control of the NFC East, and today they earned their most impressive win yet.

The Jaguars fall to 7-3, and despite the loss they’re still the overwhelming favorites to win the AFC South. This loss will hurt in the AFC playoff seeding, however, as they’re now long shots to earn the No. 1 seed.

Both the Giants and the Jaguars look like playoff teams. This was a hard-fought game between two opponents that expect to still be playing well into January. And maybe February.

sports.title: Broncos move to 8-2 with 38-24 victory over Raiders
sports.summary: A pick-six off of Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter sealed Denver's win.
sports.body:
A pick-six off of Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter sealed the Broncos’ 38-24 victory.

The Raiders got down 17-0 early but came back to tie the game up at 17-17 midway through the third quarter. The Broncos responded by ripping off a pair of touchdowns, one of which came off a turnover on downs in Denver territory when Mendoza’s pass on fourth-and-2 fell incomplete.

But Las Vegas wasn’t done, scoring on a 7-yard pass from Mendoza with 4:29 left in the contest. Then the defense got a stop, setting up a potential game-tying drive just before the two-minute warning.

However, after that short break, Mendoza was looking for Tre Tucker when his pass was instead picked off by Ja’Quan McMillan — who returned it for a game-sealing, 35-yard pick-six.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix finished the contest 19-of-35 for 225 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Evan Engram led with 74 yards on six catches. Running back Jonah Coleman had 111 yards on 24 carries plus four catches for 18 yards.

On the other side, Mendoza finished 18-of-37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one pick in his second start. He was sacked five times. His first touchdown pass went to Ashton Jeanty, who had 90 yards on five catches to go along with 79 yards on 11 carries. His 46-yard run was his longest of the season.

With the win, the Broncos move to 8-2. They’ll have a short week, as they’ll face the Steelers on the road for next week’s Black Friday game.

The Raiders fall to 4-7. They’ll be on the road again next week in primetime, with the matchup against the Browns flexed to Sunday Night Football.

sports.title: Robert Saleh: We played disgusting football on Sunday
sports.summary: The Titans were on the receiving end of a thrashing in Dallas on Sunday.
sports.body:
The Cowboys scored touchdowns on seven of their eight possessions and racked up 480 yards before kneeling out at the end of a 51-30 win. Their offense settled for three field goals in the first half and couldn’t keep up with the stream of points that the Cowboys generated over the course of the afternoon.

After the game, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that his team “took a step back today.”

“There’s a lot of things that need to change,” Saleh said, via the team’s website. “Obviously, it’s disgusting football, it’s embarrassing football. And obviously that starts with me.”

Saleh’s frustration with Sunday’s performance is evident, but the performance wasn’t totally out of left field. It was the third straight game that the Titans allowed at least 40 points and at least 459 yards, so the defensive issues were already apparent before the Cowboys full exploited them.

sports.title: Jets beat Chargers 27-24 to end five-game losing streak
sports.summary: The Jets scored on their first five possessions and then ran out the clock on the Chargers from there.
sports.body:
Geno Smith threw three touchdown passes and the Jets scored on their first five possessions of the game. Their sixth and final possession began after the Chargers cut their lead to 27-24 on the final play before the two minute warning and the Jets were able to run for a pair of first downs that allowed them to head home with their third win of the season.

The Jets’ five scoring drives were all long marches down the field that ate up clock and cut down on the Chargers’ margin for error during their own time with the ball. The Jets were 9-of-11 on third downs over the course of the afternoon and Smith’s efficient 17-of-21 passing for 176 yards was matched by a strong rushing attack.

Breece Hall had 20 carries for 86 yards and Braelon Allen chipped in 16 carries for 75 more yards. Hall caught one of Smith’s touchdowns and veteran Sterling Shepard caught the other two after coming up as a practice squad elevation to help cover for the absences of Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams.

The Chargers were fairly efficient as well and they avoided the turnovers that plagued them during their 0-8 start to the season, but a three-and-out to open the third quarter was followed by a 10-minute Jets scoring drive and the defense’s inability to get off the field didn’t leave the Chargers with enough opportunities to pick up their second win of the season.

They’ll remain in Los Angeles in Week 12 to host the reeling Patriots while the 3-8 Jets will be in Miami to try to avoid a season sweep at the hands of the Dolphins.

Facing fourth down at their own 39-yard line, the Broncos elected to go for it with a QB sneak. But Bo Nix wasn’t pushed across the line to gain, resulting in a turnover on downs. The officials reviewed it and the call was upheld.

With great field position, Las Vegas took full advantage of the opportunity, largely with the run game. Mike Washington took four consecutive carries before Mendoza faked it to him, rolled to the right, and hit Thomas in stride down the field for his second career passing touchdown.

On the injury front, Raiders defensive tackle Adam Butler (concussion) and defensive tackle Tim Keenan (knee) have been downgraded to out.

sports.body: In the immediate aftermath of the Buffalo Bills’ Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins, many will scratch their heads wondering what they watched unfold Sunday afternoon. To be clear her: What a strange win by the Bills. Buffalo’s offense barely resembled the group most have watched in 2026. It’s important to step back a moment, however, and realize that Buffalo has built a good, often great team. The Bills haven’t trailed in a game since October 18 against the Las Vegas Raiders (hat tip: Carson Hayek). Buffalo has also won three consecutive games by 17 or more points. What about the defense? Well, that group hasn’t allowed a touchdown in three straight games. It may be true that the Bills didn’t execute their most impressive game plan of the season, and that they strayed too far away from their true identity until crunch time. It’s clear that quarterback Josh Allen didn’t have his typically dominant effort against the Dolphins, even though he did throw for 304 yards, but he didn’t need to play lights out. Interestingly, Allen attempted zero rushes. In fact, during a first-half 4th & 1 situation, Allen handed the ball off to running back James Cook III, who scampered through the right side of the line to move the chains. The intent seemed clear that the move was to avoid exposing Allen to unnecessary contact, at least. That move can only work so well when you ask the quarterback to drop back 45 times. As a result, Miami’s defense hit Allen six times, sacking him on three occasions. Most believed that Buffalo would use their dominant rushing attack to try and wear down the Dolphins’ trio of backup defensive tackles in the first half. It was tough sledding early, perhaps surprisingly to Brady and the offense, and Cook had just 13 carries for 36 yards and a touchdown at halftime. Allen was forced into two consecutive interceptions late in the second quarter, with a third erased due to penalty. Then consider the decisions on special teams. sports.body:
While the Bears looked rusty coming off of their Week 10 bye, they still were able to make enough plays to defeat New Orleans 21-10 on Sunday.

Chicago got out to a 16-0 lead midway through the second quarter with a 41-yard field goal and two touchdown passes from Caleb Williams, though one of them featured a missed extra point. But the Saints narrowed that lead to six points at halftime with a 1-yard pass from Tyler Shough to Alvin Kamara paired with a 56-yard field goal from Charlie Smyth.

That, however, didn’t make up for an egregiously wide right missed field goal from 47 yards out.

The Bears then extended their lead with a 35-yard field goal from Cairo Santos midway through the third quarter. And the Bears got a safety early in the fourth quarter to close out their scoring, with Montez Sweat bringing Shough down in the end zone for a sack.

The Saints got down to Chicago’s 10-yard line after a Bears fumble in the fourth quarter, but weren’t able to connect, turning it over on downs.

With no timeouts due to failed challenges, New Orleans could only manage a 51-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter before attempting an onside kick.

As noted by the Fox broadcast, this was the Bears’ fifth consecutive game without trailing. It’s the franchise’s longest streak since 1959, when they had six such contests.

Williams ended the game 15-of-23 for 181 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.

Divisional contests are never easy, so I was instantly wary of the 16.5-point spread given Buffalo’s 8-1 record and Miami’s 1-8 record entering play. sports.title: Bills don't allow a touchdown for third straight game, beat Dolphins 26-9
sports.summary: The Bills are 9-1 heading into Thursday night's matchup with the Chiefs.
sports.body:
Miami picked up 185 yards over the entire game and never got the ball into the end zone, which makes it three straight games where the Bills have allowed nothing more than a field goal. The 26-9 win was their sixth in a row and their 9-1 record matches the best 10-game start in franchise history, but things should get tougher in Week 12.

Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord was making his second NFL start, which fits in with recent trends for the AFC East frontrunner. They have also faced the likes of Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Cade Klubnik for all or large portions of their four wins after their Week Seven bye, but Thursday night’s game against the Chiefs will force the defense to tangle with Patrick Mahomes.

That will force the defense to clean up any loose ends and the Bills offense will be looking to do the same over the next few days. The Bills never punted on Sunday, but Josh Allen threw a pair of interceptions and five of their drives ended with field goal attempts rather than touchdowns. That is enough to outlast teams like the Dolphins, but finishing off their bid for the top seed in the AFC is going to take more emphatic efforts over the rest of the season.

Running back James Cook should play a leading role in that effort. Cook ran 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown, which pushed him over 1,000 rushing yards for the season and gives him nine straight games with at least 75 rushing yards and a score. Per CBS, that’s the longest streak of its kind in NFL history.

Allen finished 27-of-45 for 304 yards and a touchdown that went to wide receiver DJ Moore. Moore had eight catches for 91 yards and Khalil Shakir added five catches for 101 yards. On the defensive side, Greg Rousseau had a pair of sacks to move him to 10 for the season and safety Damar Hamlin had his first interception of the season.

The Dolphins will be back in Miami for Week 12 and they’ll host the Jets in a bid to sweep the season series from their divisional rivals. That won’t have any impact on the playoff race, but both of those teams have at least one eye on the draft order as they play out the string on a losing season.

Patrick Mahomes’ 18-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Worthy early in the fourth quarter put the game away with a 27-point lead.

That was also Mahomes’ last pass, as Justin Fields came in to play the rest of the game.

Mahomes finished the contest 27-of-39 for 324 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. It’s the first time this season Mahomes has thrown for at least three touchdowns with no interceptions in consecutive games.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in touchdown receptions by a tight end, trailing only Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez. He finished the contest with six catches for 74 yards with a pair of touchdowns.

Once again starting in place of the injured Kenneth Walker, rookie Emmett Johnson had another strong performance with 105 yards rushing on 23 carries with a touchdown. He also caught four passes for 38 yards.

On the other side, quarterback Josh Johnson was able to get a little something going midway through the first half with a 10-play touchdown drive. But other than that, the Cardinals’ offense was overmatched and overwhelmed throughout the afternoon. Johnson finished 18-of-31 for 155 yards with a touchdown. Arizona did not have much of a running game, with Bam Knight gaining 35 yards on seven carries and Tyler Allgeier rushing for 23 yards on seven carries.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills defense has spent the past several weeks keeping opponents out of the end zone. On Sunday, against the Miami Dolphins, that stretch of defensive football put the 2026 Bills in the franchise record book. Buffalo broke the record at the end of the first half, pushing it to 40 straight drives without allowing a touchdown, and added to it in the second half. Miami didn’t score a touchdown and the drive record stands at 43. The Bills haven’t allowed a touchdown in three straight games, a first for the franchise. This streak began during Buffalo’s Week 8 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, following a first-quarter touchdown run by Derrick Henry. The Bills held Baltimore without another touchdown, then kept the Minnesota Vikings and New York Jets out of the end zone entirely. Against Minnesota, Buffalo allowed just two field goals in a 23-6 Week 9 win. Last week, the Jets managed four field goals in a 31-12 loss, despite moving the ball into the red zone twice. By the time the Bills returned home to face Miami, they had gone 33 consecutive opponent drives without allowing a touchdown, the longest active streak in the NFL. It was also quite a turnaround for a defense that had struggled through the first six games of the season. Buffalo allowed an average of 28.5 points per game during that stretch, but held its next three opponents to a combined 28 points. Head coach Joe Brady credited improved communication and a better understanding of the defensive scheme for the change. And while the Bills have continued to give up yards at times, they’ve been much better at keeping those yards from turning into touchdowns. Buffalo started the game forcing punts on Miami’s first two possessions. They then allowed the Dolphins to move the ball, but eventually the Bills’ defense settled in and forced Miami to settle for a field goal. The Dolphin’s fourth drive ended in a punt before their fifth got them close enough to put three more points on the board. That stop tied the 1999 Bills’ team. The record breaking drive was just one play. Damar Hamlin picked off Kyle McCord’s pass on the first play of Miami’s sixth offensive drive of the game. The previous franchise record belonged to the 1999 Bills, who went 38 consecutive defensive possessions without allowing a touchdown. sports.title: Bills lead Dolphins 20-6 at halftime
sports.summary: The Bills have a big game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, but they haven't gotten caught looking ahead against the Dolphins this Sunday.
sports.body:
Josh Allen hit wide receiver DJ Moore for a touchdown and running back James Cook ran for another score as the Bills extended their lead to 20-3 in the second quarter. The Dolphins capitalized on a Josh Allen interception to cut the lead to 20-6 and the Bills’ bid to pad their lead appeared to end with an interception by safety Zayne Anderson with 18 seconds to play in the half.

Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord returned the favor one play later, however. His pass to wide receiver Chris Bell was picked off by safety Damar Hamlin and the play proved to be doubly painful for the Dolphins when Bell needed medical attention after a big collision with Hamlin.

The Bills got the ball near midfield and Allen threw his third interception of the half, but it was wiped off the board by a defensive holding penalty. The Bills completed a short pass to Moore on the untimed final down of the second quarter.

Allen’s first interception came when Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson tipped a pass that fluttered into the hands of rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez and Rodriguez took the ball back to the Buffalo 22-yard-line, but Greg Rousseau’s second sack of the game and his 10th of the season meant that they wouldn’t be able to turn it into six points.

It was an erratic half for Allen, who went into the break 15-of-30 for 173 yards, but a two-touchdown lead attests to the difference between the overall quality of the two teams on the field in Buffalo.

sports.title: Bears lead Saints 16-10 at halftime
sports.summary: The Saints have put some pressure on the Bears, but Chicago still has a 16-7 lead over New Orleans at halftime.
sports.body:
Chicago took a 16-0 lead with a Cairo Santos 41-yard field goal, a 3-yard touchdown reception from D’Andre Swift, and a 15-yard scoring strike from Caleb Williams to Colston Loveland. Santos missed the extra point on Loveland’s touchdown wide right to keep the score at 16-0.

But the Saints then got on the board with a 1-yard run from Alvin Kamara. They could’ve scored three more points, but Charlie Smyth’s 47-yard attempt was extremely wide right and no good.

Smyth made up for it with a 56-yard field goal to end the half, sending the ball right down the middle, hitting the crossbar to send it through the uprights.

New Orleans QB Tyler Shough finished the first half 9-of-17 passing for 93 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

On the other side, Williams is 10-of-16 for 113 yards with two touchdowns and a pick.

Bears running back Roschon Johnson is doubtful to return with an ankle injury.

New Orleans will have a chance to take the lead to start the third quarter, as the Saints will receive the second-half kickoff.

sports.title: Travis Kelce has two TDs, Chiefs lead Cardinals 27-7 at halftime

Kelce’s first score in the first quarter moved him past Rob Gronkowski on the all-time list for most TD receptions by a tight end, putting Kelce at No. 3 behind Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez.

He scored his second in the second quarter, catching a 22-yard pass over the middle from Patrick Mahomes.

Kelce finished the first half with six receptions for 74 yards with two scores.

The tight end’s performance was emblematic of the dominance of Kansas City’s offensive unit, as the Chiefs scored on each of their five possessions in the half.

Emmett Johnson, starting for Kenneth Walker for the second consecutive game, rushed for 66 yards on 16 carries with a touchdown. He also had three receptions for 46 yards in the first 30 minutes.

Mahomes is 21-of-31 for 233 yards with two touchdowns and no picks.

On the other side, Josh Johnson — starting in place of the injured Carson Beck — was able to engineer one scoring drive early in the second quarter. But Arizona’s offense has otherwise had a lot of trouble doing much of anything. Johnson finished the first half 8-of-12 for 69 yards with a touchdown.

sports.body: There are plenty of ways to measure Josh Allen’s place in NFL history. Passing yards, passing touchdowns, rushing touchdowns. Pick a category, and the Buffalo Bills quarterback is probably climbing the leaderboard. But there is one particular combination of accomplishments that no player in NFL history has managed to put together. Until now. Allen has officially moved into the NFL’s top 50 all-time passing yards leaders. He entered Sunday’s game needing 20 yards to pass Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner, who finished his career with 32,344 yards. Allen started the day completing two of his first three passes. The first was a 9-yard pass to DJ Moore. The second was 32-yard shot to Khalil Shakir. But, of course, he didn’t stop there. After five straight incompletions spread across two drives, Allen hit Ray Davis for a six yard completion and then found Dawson Knox across the middle for another 23. Those 70 yards had Allen leap both Warner and Cam Newton (32, 382) to land at number 49 on the NFL’s all-time list. Moving into the top 50 in passing yards did more than give Allen another name to cross off the leaderboard. It made him the first player in NFL history to rank among the top 50 in career passing yards, passing touchdowns, and rushing touchdowns. Here’s where Allen stands on each of the NFL’s all-time lists: * Passing yards: Number 49. (Next up is Ken Anderson with 32,838 yards) * Passing touchdowns: Tied at Number 38. Both Allen and Donovan McNabb have thrown 344 scoring passes. * Rushing touchdowns: Number 16 with 90. Allen’s place on the rushing touchdown list is the fun one, considering that the 15 players ahead of him are all running backs. His 90 career rushing touchdowns are already the most by a quarterback in NFL history, and he’s just one away from joining the top 12 all-time. The three-category milestone adds to a résumé that already includes an NFL MVP award (2024 NFL season), multiple Pro Bowl selections, and a collection of league and franchise records. Allen is definitely making his case for a future in Canton – all that’s missing is that Lombardi trophy.

That cut the Chiefs’ lead in half, making the score 14-7 with 9:48 left in the second quarter.

The Cardinals weren’t able to do anything offensively in the first quarter, going three-and-out. The team barely got the ball back in the first period, as Kansas City went on two long touchdown drives of 11 and 16 plays.

We’ll see if the Cardinals can keep it up and really make it a game in Kansas City.

Along the way, cornerback Jacob Parrish suffered a back injury. He has headed to the locker room, and he’s questionable to return.

sports.summary: It wasn't a good start for the Panthers today against the Ravens.
sports.body:
Carolina started its first drive deep in its own territory after a Baltimore punt, and on the Panthers’ third play, Bryce Young dropped into the end zone and was sacked by Mike Green for a safety.

On the subsequent Baltimore drive, the Ravens pulled out all the stops: Derrick Henry took the snap with quarterback Jacoby Brissett lined up as a wide receiver. Henry gave the ball to Justice Hill, who ran to the outside and gave it to Brissett, who launched it downfield to a wide open Rashod Bateman for a 52-yard touchdown.

Brissett has now thrown touchdown passes for seven different teams in his career, and it’s now 9-0 Ravens.

The Panthers enter today’s game with a 4-5 record and the Ravens are 4-6, but the Panthers are actually in first place in the NFC South, while the Ravens are probably out of playoff contention. That didn’t stop the Ravens from coming to play.

sports.body:

Kelce capped the Chiefs’ first drive with an 8-yard touchdown catch, giving Kansas City an early 7-0 lead over Arizona.

The score also moved Kelce past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in touchdowns by a tight end. Only Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez are ahead of Kelce on the list.

The possession lasted 11 plays and went 72 yards to the end zone, taking 5:14 off the clock.

Patrick Mahomes was 4-of-5 on the drive for 36 yards, converting a pair of third downs. He hit Rashee Rice for a 15-yard gain on one third down and the touchdown to Kelce was the second.

sports.body: It’s finally time, Rumblers! The Buffalo Bills get their first crack at the Miami Dolphins today, and the two teams couldn’t be much further apart if they tried. Today’s game is an important one for both clubs, but the Bills have very different goals. Buffalo will look to improve on its 1-1 record versus the AFC East, and to maintain sole possession of first place in the AFC. Miami is looking to build upon its first victory last Sunday, and winning against the conference-leading Bills would go a long way in building confidence for the rebuilding team. Buffalo will have to rely on quite a few backups today based on the Bills’ Week 11 inactive list. Starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams were ruled out Friday afternoon. The Bills will also be without starting tight end Dalton Kincaid, whose prior “doubtful” game-day designation now turns into “out” for Week 11. Despite showing up as “questionable” due to a late injury on Saturday, defensive tackle Ed Oliver is not among Buffalo’s inactive players. We’ll see how much he’s able to contribute this afternoon. Make no mistake, this is a very important game for the Bills despite the circumstances of their opponent. Buffalo will have a short week of rest and to prepare for their Week 12 opponents, the Kansas City Chiefs, who they host in primetime on Thanksgiving night. A win today would also give Buffalo its first victory in their NFL/Nike Rivals uniforms. Will head coach Joe Brady and the Bills’ offense look to feature the ground-and-pound rushing attack today, in an effort to shorten the game and wear down Miami? It’s work well in recent weeks against other opponents, and running back James Cook III has a goal to hit 2,000 yards on the ground this season. With that all in mind, here’s your open thread for Bills-Dolphins in Week 11. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: Something strange happened here at Buffalo Rumblings following the Buffalo Bills’ win against the New York Jets. It was the team’s first win against an AFC East foe this season (now 1-1), and the victory allowed them to retain their lead in the AFC playoff race thanks to an 8-1 overall record. Yet for some reason, there was a drop in confidence among some Rumblers who responded to our latest poll. Heading into the game versus the Jets, fan confidence was at 94%. A week later, just ahead of a home game with the Miami Dolphins, that confidence number has dropped to 89%. I blame the quality of opponent, rather than the way in which the Bills won. After all, winning, no matter how it looks, is the only thing that matters in the NFL. [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/Bills_1_111626.png?quality=90&strip=all] I’m left wondering if it’s the situation in the rest of the AFC that has some in Bills Mafia concerned about the season. There are four other teams that remain serious threats to Buffalo’s one-seed goal. We asked readers about that this week, wondering which AFC team is the biggest threat to the Bills’ hopes of securing a playoff bye. I think recency bias prevail here in the results. Leading the way are the Cincinnati Bengals (43%), a team that doesn’t face Buffalo in the regular season. In second with 39% of the vote are the Jacksonville Jaguars — another team the Bills don’t face in the current regular season. There’s a precipitous drop after those teams, surprisingly. Just 10% of people saying that the Kansas City Chiefs are the biggest threat to Buffalo. Meanwhile, only 8% of those polled say the Broncos remain the Bills’ biggest challengers to the one seed. Why do I find surprise in these results? Yes, the Bengals and Jaguars are red-hot right now. Yet, I wonder if some people thought about the direct threat the Chiefs and Broncos represent to the Bills. Remember, Buffalo will face Kansas City (at home) on (equally) short rest/prep for Week 12. They play a road game at the Denver Broncos in Week 16, another major U.S. holiday. The Chiefs and Broncos have already played each other twice in 2026, splitting the series 1-1, which means there’s no longer a chance either team can acutely unseat the other before the playoffs. sports.body: The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Sterling Shepard has been elevated to the active roster twice this season before today. He has been targeted twice by the Jets, with one reception good for three yards. The Jets needed another body at wide receiver with Cooper out. The team has Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell active, but behind those two are Tim Patrick and Malik McClain, who are unlikely to provide much value. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season. Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

sports.title: The Week 11 afternoon schedule is short on must-see games
sports.summary: As the NFL's haves and the have-nots continue to declare themselves, it's becoming challenging at times to find compelling games.
sports.body:
And while the coming week has five of them in national, standalone windows (Vikings-49ers, Packers-Rams, Bears-Lions, Chiefs-Bills, and Broncos-Steelers), the eleventh Sunday is a bit lacking. To say the least.

In the early window, three of the seven games feature double-digit spreads. The 8-1 Bills (-16.5) host the 1-8 Dolphins, who don’t have their starting quarterback. The 7-2 Chiefs (-15.5) host the 3-7 Cardinals, who are down to their fourth quarterback of the season — and the third in three weeks.

None of the early games feature two teams with winning records. Bucs-Lions is arguably the most compelling of the window, given the potential for Detroit stepping into a trap four days before the Thanksgiving showdown against the Bears.

The late time slot is led by the 7-2 Jaguars (-6) at the 5-3-1 Giants. It’s the only game of the weekend featuring a pair of division leaders.

Although it’s impossible in May to know how the various games of a given schedule will look in late November (Steelers-Eagles had the potential on paper to be the best game of the day), it’s a convenient time for a subpar Sunday. With millions still scratching their GTA itch, they can fully focus on Vice City this afternoon before the Vikings and 49ers square off tonight in Mexico City.
